skill.name: blocklet-converter
skill.description: Convert static web apps and Next.js projects into ArcBlock blocklets with generated configuration, assets, metadata, and validation steps.
skill.summary: Convert static and Next.js web projects into ArcBlock Blocklet packages.
skill.author: ArcBlock

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, documentation examples, runtime environment variables, or a reviewed PNG logo. The confirmed issues are expected operational risks: the workflow runs project install/build and Blocklet CLI commands, and one template references the ArcBlock store URL.

remediation.issue: Project install and build commands execute local project code.
remediation.suggestion: Ask users to review package scripts and confirm trust in the project before running install or build steps.

remediation.issue: Blocklet CLI commands create release artifacts in the target project.
remediation.suggestion: Document that verification and bundling should run only in the intended project directory with trusted local tooling.

remediation.issue: The static template hardcodes the ArcBlock store endpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the store endpoint documented or configurable so users understand the remote deployment dependency.

content.user_title: Convert Web Apps to ArcBlock Blocklets
content.value_statement: Packaging a web app as a Blocklet requires several configuration files and CLI checks. This skill guides conversion for static and Next.js projects using an existing DID.
actual_capabilities: Detects static web apps and Next.js projects from package files, entry points, and framework configuration.
Requires a supplied Blocklet DID and applies it to generated metadata.
Generates or copies README, logo, entry script, and blocklet.yml assets.
Runs build, metadata validation, and bundle commands when the conversion flow requires them.
Emits parseable project title and description markers for calling tools.
limitations: Supports only static web apps and Next.js projects, not backend services.
Requires a valid pre-generated Blocklet DID from the user.
Depends on local package managers, project dependencies, and the Blocklet CLI.
Build or bundle failures must be fixed in the source project.

use_cases.title: Package a Static Site
use_cases.description: Convert a built static website into a Blocklet with metadata, logo, README, and bundle validation.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Next.js App
use_cases.description: Add the required server entry file and Blocklet template for a production Next.js package.

use_cases.title: Validate Release Readiness
use_cases.description: Check project type, output paths, metadata, and bundling steps before publishing a Blocklet release.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Static App
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner conversion for a simple web project
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this static web app to an ArcBlock Blocklet using DID {did}. Create required files, validate metadata, and stop if the build fails.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Next.js App
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate conversion for a Next.js project
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare this Next.js project as an ArcBlock Blocklet using DID {did}. Add the server entry file, apply the template, and run verification.

prompt_templates.title: Check Before Conversion
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this project for Blocklet readiness. Identify project type, missing files, unsupported backend dependencies, build steps, and blocking issues before conversion.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Workspace Package
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced conversion inside a larger repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert the web package at {package_path} using DID {did}. Work only in that directory, preserve existing metadata, and report blocking errors.

output_examples.input: A Vite React project with a valid DID and a working build script.
output: Detected a static web app and extracted user-facing project metadata.
Generated Blocklet configuration, copied the default logo, and preserved existing README content.
Validated metadata and created a release bundle with the Blocklet CLI.

output_examples.input: A Next.js project with a valid DID and production dependencies installed.
output: Detected a Next.js app and used the Next.js Blocklet template.
Copied the production server entry file into the project root.
Ran metadata validation and created a simple release bundle.

output_examples.input: A repository with no package file, web entry point, or framework configuration.
output_examples.output: Stopped before making changes because no supported web application was detected.

best_practices: Review package scripts before allowing dependency installation or build commands.
Provide a valid Blocklet DID and confirm the project directory before starting.
Keep generated titles, descriptions, and output paths accurate before bundling.
anti_patterns: Running conversion in an untrusted project without inspecting scripts first.
Using this skill for backend APIs, workers, or services outside the supported scope.
Reusing one DID or generic metadata across unrelated applications.

faq.question: What project types does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports static web apps and Next.js projects. Backend frameworks are outside its supported scope.

faq.question: Do I need a Blocklet DID first?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill expects a pre-generated DID and stops if the DID is missing or invalid.

faq.question: Can it create required Blocklet files?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create blocklet.yml, add a default logo, generate README content, and add a Next.js entry script.

faq.question: Does it run commands on my project?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow can run dependency installation, build, metadata validation, and bundle commands.

faq.question: What happens if the build fails?
faq.answer: The workflow stops and reports the build error. The source project must be fixed before conversion continues.

faq.question: Is it safe to use on any repository?
faq.answer: Use it only on trusted projects. Install and build scripts can execute code from the local repository.
